notes: PvP Pad v4 on Robinhood Chain (4663), using the accepted IMD-only implementation based on identity-md-launches/launch-1832-donotbuy @a9a48cb4b458f35160da7ec0693e4b422be684ca. These five applications deploy atomically in the listed constructor dependency order with zero ETH. PadToken and PadGame are sealed templates with no constructor arguments; deployment mints no tokens and sets no token name or symbol. The supplied name nobuy does not create a deployment token. PvPPad receives $owner and the two template addresses. PadLiquidity receives the inherited PoolManager 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951, this PvPPad and IMD 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, with no pool-id argument. KingOfThePad receives this PvPPad, this PadLiquidity and $owner as dev. Owner and dev both resolve to the launch owner. PadLiquidity binds itself to PvPPad; KingOfThePad binds itself to both earlier applications during construction. Constructors call only earlier manifest contracts and require no live external dependency. Deployment creates no game clone, hook, pool or distributor and includes no initialization, openPad or other follow-up call. All tokens, including PvP, are created later through the pad. Later application use includes openPad(salt), owner-only for 30 days then permissionless, followed by IMD-funded games and direct coin/IMD graduation. IMD has 18 decimals and unverified bridged-token source; exact receipt checks and optional ERC20 returns are supported. If IMD transfers stop, the pad's IMD waits. The inherited PoolManager address is configuration, not evidence of live verification. See docs/AUDIT.md, docs/TEST-REPORT.md and docs/VERIFY.md for the accepted implementation, local gas evidence and verification handoff. Legal review and an independent audit are required before public launch.
